# Provider self-renewal audit — 2026-11-09

Drew's rule (2026-11-09 20:42 CST): **all the providers renew themselves.** Every OAuth/token credential must refresh itself automatically; a provider dying on an expired token because renewal was missing, mis-targeted, or unprovisioned is a defect. Tonight produced three instances of that defect class — openai.main (sync wrote to the wrong door; fixed, fork PR #2237), _claude (credential blanked Nov 7; restored by hand), _antigravity (client secret never provisioned; fixed, PRs #8098/#8099). This audit checks **every** door against the rule so the class is closed, not just tonight's three instances.

Method (all reads 2026-11-10 ~02:45–03:00Z, laptop, generation 551, fork build ff9858a = deployed HEAD): live config pair `opencode.jsonc` (17 providers), credential store (24 rows, metadata only — no values read), deployed source (`packages/core/src/credential/codex-sync.ts`, `packages/core/src/integration.ts` resolve path, `packages/ai/src/providers/*-auth.ts`, `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/{openai,opencode}.ts`), CLI credential files (timestamps/lengths only), route_attempt serving evidence (last 24h), quota gatherer records.

## How renewal works in this fork (the two paths)

- **In-provider refresh:** `Integration.connection.resolve` refreshes any stored OAuth credential within 5 min of expiry, when its method implements `refresh` — **unless** the credential is stamped `externalRefresh`, in which case an external owner is the sole refresher (by design, to avoid rotating a shared refresh-token lineage twice).
- **External-owner sync:** CodexSync runs every 1 min, copies `~/.codex/auth.json` into the stored credential **whose account ID matches the file's account** (selectTarget), and stamps it `externalRefresh`. One account's tokens are never written into another account's credential.

## Findings

1. **Zero CANNOT-RENEW defects among live doors.** After tonight's three fixes, every serving door either self-renews, holds a static key, or has a configured renewal that has not yet had its first natural test.
2. **Three SELF-RENEWS-UNPROVEN doors, each with a dated acceptance check:** opencode-go.popesdrew (first refresh due at the 2026-12-03 expiry approach), _claude (first rotation due at the 2026-11-10T10:28:53Z access expiry — today), _muse (re-mint unobserved; account-token expiry uninstrumented, watched by the meta-renewal validator). 4. **Quota-side browser sessions are a separate surface**, already owned by #6120 (OpenDesign keeper landed; Meta portal re-capture requirement sits on #6079; ClinePass dashboard adapter dormant by design). sub-20 AA II pull → beam-plan's scout seat becomes a right-sizing flag
candidate.* This is a hypothesis for the controlled-test mechanism (#1342),

items.body:
## What is broken, in plain words

Fleet sessions are being killed by the OpenCode client's 10-second first-output deadline. When a scheduled lane wave seats ~10 sessions inside a minute onto the same few workhorse doors, the doors queue past 10s, **every candidate in the route trips the deadline in the same turn**, and the turn ends `failed` instead of waiting out the route cooldown and retrying a live leg. The session is lost mid-task: a lane that was checkpointing, sweeping, or binding a queue task simply stops.

## Evidence (laptop server 127.0.0.1:13420, opencode.db, window 2026-11-08T18:10Z–2026-11-09T02:10Z)

**81 sessions ended `failed` with the identical error** `provider.transport` / `"No response output within 10000ms"`:

| hour (UTC) | deaths |
|---|---|
| 17 | 18 |
| 18 | 30 |
| 19 | 7 |
| 20 | 26 |

Named sessions (verbatim `idle.outcome` rows):

- `ses_e5e41f73dc2ffeXtjBHfPlEsgd` — Queue lane (scheduled) - code 20:00, died 20:08 mid-checkpoint; last text: `repo-queue: primary queue store failed on /checkpoint (exit 5): checkpoint_task: task 14030 is not claimed by repo-worker-code`
- `ses_e5e41f6c26cffed2YLdfEQyJBz` — Queue lane (scheduled) - code 20:00, died 20:09 immediately after blocking task 14029
- `ses_e5e42091170ffef0WR74Z0IPyW` — Fleet conductor 19:40, died 20:12 mid-sweep (it was polling post-nudge session activity)
- `ses_e5e41fa5585ffeFA3Q6M5XsU9J` — explore subagent under task 13835, died 20:00 ("No response output within 10000ms")

**The route does fail over — and still runs out.** `route_attempt` for `ses_e5e42091170ffef0WR74Z0IPyW` (4 consecutive timeout rows, then the turn ends):

```
1794190242512  opencode-go.developing-today-0/deepseek-v4.1-flash  timeout  Transport  Timeout
1794190255506  opencode-go.developing-today-0/deepseek-v4.1-flash  timeout  Transport  Timeout
1794190271205  opencode-go.popesdrew/deepseek-v4.1-flash             timeout  Transport  Timeout
1794190294012  opencode-go.drewrypope/deepseek-v4.1-flash            timeout  Transport  Timeout
```

**The deadline is being hit at a real rate, and the legs routinely exceed it.** 8h `route_attempt` totals:

| provider/model | success | Transport/Timeout |
|---|---|---|
| openai.main/gpt-6-luna | 19,757 | 1,166 |
| opencode-go.developing-today-0/deepseek-v4.1-flash | 2,085 | 407 |
| _muse/muse-spark-1.3-contributor | 1,464 | 158 |
| _vibe/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017 | 4,194 | 217 |

Observed first-token maxima in the last 2h: gpt-6-luna **15,738 ms**, deepseek-v4.1-flash **10,185 ms**, muse-spark **10,428 ms** — i.e. these legs cross a 10 s deadline as a matter of course, and a burst pushes every door over it at once.

**The waves are the trigger.** Ten scheduled code lanes started between 20:00:01 and 20:00:52 local on the same `opencode-route/workhorse` chain (`workhorse-ordered` → `deepseek-flash-plan` → `workhorse-weighted`); 26 sessions died in the 20:00 hour.

## Why this is not #4370 or #3325

- #4370 (closed completed 2026-11-08T10:51Z) was closed on the verdict that per-leg shedding was "superseded" because `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` was retired. That premise is false at main today: `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` is tracked, `f61b2af25e` ("fix(route-proxy): timeout each leaf first response") is an ancestor of `origin/main`, and the death class returned at 81/8h after the closure.
- #3325 (open) is the quota-exhausted-leg class (429 / muse-spark). This is the first-output-deadline class, which reaches the session as `provider.transport`, not `provider.rate-limit`.

## Acceptance test (one line)

Replaying a 10-session scheduled lane wave on `opencode-route/workhorse`, **zero sessions end with `provider.transport: No response output within 10000ms`** — either the deadline is sized above the observed leg p99 (or disabled for this chain), or a turn whose candidates all trip it retries after the route cooldown and completes, shown by a `route_attempt` timeout row set followed by a success row in the same turn.

## Pointers for the fix

- Client: `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts` builds the synthetic `TransportError` for the deadline (code `Timeout`) and `packages/core/src/model-route.ts` defaults `firstTokenTimeoutMs` to 10_000. The fork may need to retry after cooldown when the last candidate times out.
- Config: `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` sets no `health.firstTokenTimeoutMs` on the workhorse chain, so the 10 s default applies to every leg.
- Concurrency: the scheduled lane wave starts ~10 sessions inside a minute on the same three DeepSeek doors (see also #6533, claimant cap 36 saturated).

items.title: quota: no labelled opencode-go.popesdrew row — the account's Console measurement publishes as the unlabelled opencode-go aggregate
items.body:
## Symptom

The quota gatherer's record (`~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-current.json`, 15-minute ticks) carries labelled per-account rows for two of the three OpenCode Go accounts — `opencode-go.drewrypope` and `opencode-go.developing-today-0` — plus ONE unlabelled `opencode-go` row. There is no labelled `opencode-go.popesdrew` row, so that account's windows cannot be read or steered per-account. The three Go accounts are seated 1:1:1 in the deepseek-flash-plan tier of workhorse-ordered, so per-account steering matters.

Census 2026-11-10 (quota-current.json generatedAt 2026-11-10T20:30:08Z, all rows fresh-measured in that tick):

- `opencode-go.drewrypope` — 5h 0% / weekly 100% / monthly 100% (monthly resets 2026-12-03T03:02:35Z)
- `opencode-go.developing-today-0` — 5h 0% / weekly 100% / monthly 54% (monthly resets 2026-12-08T22:09:41Z)
- `opencode-go` (unlabelled, no credentialId) — weekly 100% / monthly 100%, credits_balance $0.00, resets 2026-11-16T00:00Z / 2026-12-03T17:35:51Z

## Root cause (wire-verified on the laptop, 2026-11-10)

The unlabelled row IS popesdrew's measurement, unattributed:

- popesdrew is enrolled as a **Console OAuth device sign-in** (credential `cred_bh5LJo8s26zwYccj8tDnC3LP1x`, org `org_01M6H7986JGCDR5H81QXPFJW2J`, popesdrew@gmail.com, token expiry 2026-12-03T17:42:29Z) stored under its **own instance integration** `opencode-go.popesdrew`. The other two accounts hold API-key credentials under their instance integrations. The same Console sign-in also exists as the shared `opencode` integration's active row.
- The gatherer's single source is the opencode fork's quota subcommand (`opencode quota --json`, fork `packages/ai/src/quota`). Its base per-credential walk for `opencode-go` reads only the credential aliases `opencode` + `opencode-go` — so it measures popesdrew's account **through the shared `opencode` row** and emits it as the bare, unlabelled `opencode-go` result. Proof the numbers are popesdrew's: a direct Console status call with that credential returns week used 3,006,253,692 / 3,000,000,000 micro-cents (100%, resets 2026-11-16T00:00Z), month 6,006,253,692 / 6,000,000,000 (100%, resets 2026-12-03T17:35:51Z — exactly the unlabelled row's reset), billing balance 0 ($0.00 — exactly the unlabelled row's balance), fiveHour meter present but idle (used 0, resetsAt null — the Console parser drops a meter with no reset, which is why the unlabelled row has no 5h window while the API-key rows do).
- The instance path never rescues it: `opencode-go` did not set `foldInstanceCredentials` (only Codex did), so configured instances were never folded into the base answer; and the row-usability verdict re-keys an instance row under the base id (`opencode-go`), where a Console sign-in reads as neither Console credential (that lookup keys on the shared `opencode` integration) nor API key — so the instance is judged unusable, excluded from the configured listing, and an explicit ask for `opencode-go.popesdrew` answers `Not configured` (verified live).

## Fix

In the opencode fork's quota module (the gatherer's single source), with the OpenChamber quota lib (the same module's original home, still used by OpenChamber surfaces) mirrored:

1. `opencode-go` provider sets `foldInstanceCredentials: true` — configured Go instances fold into the base answer, one labelled row per account, the pattern Codex already uses for openai.main / openai.alternate.

## Symptom

The quota record (`~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-current.json`) carries three **fresh-measured** provider rows for the OpenCode **Zen** door family —

- `opencode.drewrypope`
- `opencode.popesdrew`
- `opencode.developing-today-0`

— but none of them is registered in the attribution the AI Plans & Usage Space is built from: `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts` (`POOL_SPECS` / `SHELL_POOLS`) and `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-gather-map.ts` (`GO_*`/`OPENAI_*` split service-id constants, `CANONICAL_PROVIDER_IDS`). The Space therefore has no registered pool for these measured meters (the same defect class that hid the third Go account before #7835).

Found by the standing Plans Space freshness keeper (hourly check 2026-11-15T08:23:40Z).

## Evidence

Record: `generatedAt 2026-11-15T08:15:07.851Z`, `source opencode-quota`, heartbeat `ok`.

Measured rows (all `state: ok`):

| providerId | measuredAt | 5h resetsAt | weekly | monthly |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode.drewrypope` | 2026-11-15T08:15:37.771Z | 08:43:50Z | 100% | 100%, resets 2026-12-03T03:02:35Z |
| `opencode.popesdrew` | 2026-11-15T08:15:37.971Z | 08:43:36Z | 100% | 100%, resets 2026-12-03T17:35:51Z |
| `opencode.developing-today-0` | 2026-11-15T08:15:38.101Z | 08:43:39Z | 100% | 54%, resets 2026-12-08T22:09:41Z |

**Every window is numerically identical to the corresponding `opencode-go.*` row in the same tick** (same 5h reset seconds, same weekly/monthly percentages, same monthly reset instants). That is the key design question: the Zen door appears to read the *same plan meters* as the Go door for each workspace, so a naive registration of three new pools would render duplicate meters on the Space under a second id, while not registering them leaves the measured set incomplete.

Where registration is missing, verified against `origin/main` at `5b419f0c7b` (== local HEAD):

- `quota-extract.ts` `POOL_SPECS` contains only `opencode-go.drewrypope`, `opencode-go.popesdrew`, `opencode-go.developing-today-0` (lines ~576-598); no bare `opencode.*` ids, and `SHELL_POOLS` has no entry either.

1. **Alias** the Zen rows onto the existing Go pools (`opencode.drewrypope` -> `opencode-go.drewrypope`, etc.) via `canonicalProviderId` / a service-id map in `quota-gather-map.ts`, so the measured set is complete without duplicating meters; or

- Every providerId present in `quota-current.json providers[]` is either registered in `POOL_SPECS`/`SHELL_POOLS` or explicitly canonicalized/aliased, with `opencode.*` no longer unaccounted for.

items.body:
## Problem

`demotedPairs()` in `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs:339` is the route proxy's only leg-health gate (`applyDemotion(candidates, demotedPairs())` at line 936). It demotes a `(provider, model)` pair after ≥3 failures in 4 hours **only when the failure carries quota detail or `error_tag = 'RateLimit'`** — the SQL filter at line 347 is literally:

```sql
AND (quota IS NOT NULL OR error_tag = 'RateLimit')
```

A leg failing **every** attempt with `provider.auth` is therefore never demoted, never excluded and never reordered: it stays first-choice for new sessions and is handed out indefinitely. Today that leg is `openai.main/gpt-6-luna`.

## Evidence (2026-11-09, laptop `route_usage`, window 09:18Z–12:18Z)

| leaf | requests | failed | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openai.main/gpt-6-luna` | 3070 | **3070 (100%)** | 0 |
| `openai.alternate/gpt-6-luna` | 4 | 4 (100%) | 0 |
| `_muse/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | 3389 | 1589 (47%) | 95.3M |
| `opencode-go.developing-today-0/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 1021 | 93 (9%) | 39.0M |
| `opencode-go.popesdrew/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 283 | 31 (11%) | 10.4M |

Pool accounting from the same readout: `workhorse-weighted` **offered** `openai-plan/gpt-6-luna` **4706 times** and **chose it 3074**, while the healthy leaves above sat in the same pool and served normally. 234 sessions carried at least one of those 3070 failures.

Session-level consequence (OpenChamber attention feed): the entire **06:00, 06:20 and 06:30 CST waves** died at message 3 with the verbatim error `Provided authentication token is expired. Please try signing in again.` — including the fleet conductor, the main-CI fix trigger, the quota gatherer guardian, the builder's advocate and 8+ code lanes. That is ~40% of new workhorse sessions lost for the day, and the work each of them had claimed evaporated with them.

## Why this is not #3325 and not #5558

- **#3325** (and its parked fix task 8932 / open PR #5558) is about a session **falling through** to a live leg after a pre-content stream error. Necessary, but orthogonal: with perfect fall-through the dead leg is still first-choice for every new session and every session still burns its first attempt on it.
- **#5295** (closed) added the *quota-only* known-exhausted seating gate — same doctrine, same blind spot.
- This issue is the **demotion predicate** itself: a leg that fails 100% of attempts for any non-quota reason is not treated as unhealthy, so `route_usage`' offered-count for a dead leaf grows without bound.

Distinct code site (`demotedPairs()` filter), distinct acceptance (below).

## Acceptance criteria

- A `(provider, model)` pair with a **100% failure run** (≥ threshold attempts, zero successes) inside the demotion window is demoted/excluded from candidacy **regardless of error class** — at minimum for `provider.auth` — until it records one success. Verified in `route_usage`: the dead leaf's *offered* count stops growing while it is failing (today it was 4706 in 3h).
- Existing quota/`RateLimit` demotion behaviour is unchanged; its tests still pass.
- A session whose first attempt lands on an auth-failing leg completes a turn on a fallback leg instead of terminating at message 3 (transcript or `route_attempt` ledger evidence).

## Out of scope

- Re-signing-in / refreshing the provider credential itself — that is #7991 and is Drew's action.
- Pool weights, burn order or model choices for healthy leaves; any paid-route or PAYG switch.

## Pointers

- `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs:338-347` (`demotedPairs`), `:936` (call site)
- `bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs` (existing demotion tests to extend)
- Triage of #3325, task 14387, lane code-f — https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3325#issuecomment-6739954243
- Recurrence evidence on #3325 (auth leg, three waves lost) — https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3325#issuecomment-6739882519

A completed design is NOT a completed implementation epic; implementation children stay open until their own acceptance gates pass.

**Intrinsic urgency: 450 (High)** — ahead of normal actionable work (PM charter bands). Dispatch directive: direct Summit session, launched and verified by the orchestrator (this issue's comments carry the launch receipt).

## Authoritative sources (read as ONE intake; precedence: Drew's current instructions → dated addendum refinements → v0.3 spec baseline → decision review proposals → historical inputs)

1. **Muse handoff — Fleet CA, Credentials & Secrets** (Google Doc, modified 2026-11-12): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yeSWQvMIer92zQ4lj99TsTH2oXZem0WfH-WMYKYJpJ0
2. **Fleet v0.3 complete package** (`fleet_architecture_v0_3_complete.zip`, SHA-256 `d853a2bacf391856a863c292b21f5a224352a6681dd81fe55c422040b1fb5644`, internal SHA256SUMS all verified at intake): the governing 50-section spec (§§0–49 + Appendix A), `SECRETS_BACKEND_RESEARCH_2026-11-06.md`, `DECISION_REVIEW_AND_NEXT_STEPS.md`, `fleet_agent_handoff_prompt_v0_3.md`, `source_input_3_architectural_perspective.txt`. Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cdmoblf8yQM2NuXsR2i90N45dABU1EPo/view
3. **Secrets addendum** (architecture/performance/infrastructure follow-up, refines the package): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QkQMPYGEHbjdyMBdrcSdo4i2GKxlJYK2S3PDrvCRfVw/edit
4. **Summit coordinator handoff** (execution contract for this run): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AKDACXObRcUwmJIeCfLaGv6bxcWC00e3rYjOztk4qiY/edit
5. Companion PM charter (shared queue/dispatch conventions ONLY — the CA epic stays separate from PM implementation): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_DQwNbuRmJnITDKKJJ7A3Q0FJa-q2rkzWlz-4PyA_iw/edit

All sources are merged into the repo design directory (see the docs PR linked in comments) and staged on the laptop at `~/.local/share/fleet/intake/fleet-ca-v03-20261112/` (zip hash re-verified after transfer). Repo pinned at intake: `6a7843cae59878e10071f27440b93489053dbc68` (2026-11-12).

## Binding constraints (Drew)

- **ML-DSA-44 is the baseline signature scheme** for the CA design.
- **The Merkle-tree experiment (Cloudflare MTC) is OPTIONAL** — a separate, non-blocking controlled-stack research track; never a v1 dependency. (Handoff doc carries the full MTC analysis: inclusion proofs vs whole certs, landmark/cosigner provisioning, PQ-only separation, byte/CPU/latency comparison against the shortest conventional ML-DSA chain.)

## Scope (from the handoff doc — the CA/credentials workstream, NOT the PM-stack redesign)

Unified secret records + BWS/op/bw adapters (three DIFFERENT provider products — never conflated); daily three-way reconciliation with recoverable `zz.delete` history and false-delete prevention; audit/event journal + provider performance benchmarks; fnox library evaluation (near-term priority); SOPS/age/NixOS integration; password, SSH and iroh generation; reusable Rust APIs + the existing Fleet multicall CLI (no competing tool); PKI root/issuer/leaf lifecycle, publication, packaging, client trust and verification; nonblocking OpenBao/federation/infrastructure research.

**Reference PKI (spec controls):** four independent roots (Ed25519, P-256, RSA, ML-DSA-44), nine asymmetric root cross-certificates (ML-DSA root never signs classical roots by default), Base + Internal Web issuer sets with independent A/B partitions and eligible direct issuer cross-signatures — **20 CA key pairs / 65 CA certificate variants before leaves**. Reference expiries: roots `2050-07-07T12:00:00Z`, both issuer sets `2032-07-07T12:00:00Z` (distinct from the normal 20y/5y/90d defaults). RSA-2048 is a policy-gated compatibility option, not the default long-lived root. Root signing always requires an explicitly authorized signer source — never silently discover/exercise root keys.

**Root custody (addendum refinement):** initial roots escrowed to exactly three approved destinations — encrypted laptop storage, the authorized BWS project, the authorized 1Password vault — with integrity checks and tested restoration; NOT auto-extended to every future provider. R2 is a researched additional destination, not automatic authorization. Offline/hardware root signing is the future path; three OpenBao containers on one host are a lab, not three failure domains.

## V1 — what exists today (intake census; the Summit verifies and deepens)

- `fleet` multicall (laptop build, source rev `743966553e`) domains: queue, serve, proxy, dispatch, secrets, gh, search, laptop-agent. **No `cert`/`pki` or `generate` domain exists yet.**
- `fleet secrets get|list`: broker-first resolution with BWS fallback; name-only references; values never printed. The secrets broker is in production (see #6767 for a known broker staleness defect). No `put`, no reconciliation, no 1Password adapter in the CLI yet.
- `pkgs/fleet/crates/`: fleet, fleet-config, fleet-dispatch, fleet-proxy, fleet-proxy-proto, fleet-queue, fleet-registry, fleet-search, fleet-secrets.
- No prior Fleet v0.3 / PKI / ML-DSA / fnox / zz.delete program issues exist (searched at intake) — this epic and its domain starters are the canonical home. The earlier submission was cancelled per the handoff; nothing was launched from it.

## Safety gates (hard)

Design and synthetic proof only in this program phase. **No production CA generation or signing, no root escrow/export, no live vault writes or reconciliation, no credential rotation, no DNS/trust changes, no live service deployment** is authorized by this handoff. Synthetic fixtures must never be confused with production credentials. Design, synthetic proof, code implementation, and production rollout are separately statused.

Statement inventory (every requirement in the spec + addendum + handoffs, numbered, zero unmapped) → state-of-the-art expansion per component → versioned designs (V1 = exists today; V2+ layer) → ADRs/threat model → granular implementation/test/research issues with measurable acceptance, source IDs, boundaries, tests, rollback → batched questions recorded on THIS issue with chosen defaults (never stall). Domain starter issues are native sub-issues of this epic; the Summit files the granular children under them.

## Supervision

Orchestrator check-ins on the bound Summit session (status, questions, artifacts vs the statement inventory); stall = one nudge, then replacement, recorded here. Durable monitor: the fleet's session-minder coverage plus the supervision record in this issue's comments.

## P-384 ADR — merge remainder (lane oc-code-03, 2026-11-23)

Refs #13778 — the P-384 root-identity dated design-record PR is open (branch certprog/p384-adr, head da81369e67c005fc4ff1e6922470e9466b98a1f8; two files: the new record folder plus one doc/README.md index line). items.body:
## What this is

Route pools landed in PR #915 (design record doc/2026-10-25T21-11-31Z_design_route-pools/): tiers scout / workhorse / specialist / summit over per-model plan pools. What is missing is the policy layer and the OpenCode-native affordances. Drew directed 2026-10-29: write the escalation policy; make sure OpenCode sessions can natively change their own model; let subsessions select route pools; and make OpenCode pool-aware — prefer managed pool routes over individual model pins, without making it a hard rule.

## 1. Escalation policy (draft for Drew's approval)

- **Workhorse is the default** for all routine work (Decision 008 stands).
- **Specialist is acceptable** when any of: the task is design or deep-reasoning work; workhorse has already failed once on the same task; the code is a critical path (auth, money, data loss); the task is reviewing specialist-tier output.
- **Summit is rare** — only when: specialist has failed on the task; OR the decision is one-shot and gates many downstream tasks; OR Drew directs it. Every summit use is logged with its reason, and the daily token check-in flags summit if it exceeds ~2% of fleet tokens.
- Escalation is one tier at a time unless the failure mode clearly skips a tier.

## 2. Native model switching in OpenCode

OpenCode's own instructions must tell sessions they may change their own model mid-session when the policy above calls for it, and how: switch, note the reason in the session record, continue. No external babysitter should be required for a session to escalate itself.

## 3. Subsessions select route pools

A subsession is spawned against a route pool (tier), not a raw model, by default. The pool resolves the actual model. A specific model may be requested when the task needs a capability only that model has.

## 4. Pool awareness, managed-first

OpenCode's instructions state the pool map (tiers + plan pools) and prefer managed pool routes over individual model pins. This is a preference, not a hard requirement: pinning a specific model stays allowed, with a reason.

## Acceptance

- Policy text (with Drew's edits) landed where OpenCode reads its instructions.
- A live session demonstrably escalates its own model per policy and logs the reason.
- A subsession demonstrably spawns on a pool route.
- Summit uses show up in the daily token check-in with reasons.

items.body:
## Quota gatherer: every tick fails at import — lib dir resolves to a stale openchamber checkout parked on a queue branch

**Symptom (live 2026-11-04 evening):** `quota-gatherer.service` fails every tick in ~13ms with:

```
quota-gatherer: tick failed before providers ran: quota module import failed: auth.openCodeLocalCredentialSource is not a function. (In 'auth.openCodeLocalCredentialSource({ dbPath })', 'auth.openCodeLocalCredentialSource' is undefined)
```

(heartbeat `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-gatherer-heartbeat.json`, tickAt 2026-11-05T00:30:13Z, ok:false. Same failure at 18:18 and 18:23 CST ticks; the gatherer stall first observed 2026-11-04 ~18:30:15Z is consistent with this breakage starting earlier that day.)

**Root cause:** `resolveLibDir()` in `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts` picks the first candidate containing `quota/index.js`: `$OPENCHAMBER_LIB_DIR`, else `~/git/devtoday-openchamber/...` (doesn't exist), else `~/git/openchamber-fork/packages/web/server/lib`. The fork checkout `~/git/openchamber-fork` is currently parked on branch `queue/8357-224` (an old integration merge, e216864bf) with a dirty tree; its `packages/web/server/lib/opencode/auth.js` predates `openCodeLocalCredentialSource`. `origin/main` of the fork **has** the function (auth.js:214). The gatherer is therefore coupled to the mutable state of an unrelated work checkout — any queue lane that parks that checkout on an old branch breaks quota gathering fleet-wide, silently (heartbeat only).

**Verified workaround (used for the #5704 verification run):** a clean worktree of the fork at origin/main + `OPENCHAMBER_LIB_DIR=<worktree>/packages/web/server/lib` makes the gatherer run green.

**Fix options:**
1. Pin the deployed lib: set `OPENCHAMBER_LIB_DIR` in the quota-gatherer unit (Nix module) to a dedicated, main-tracking checkout/worktree of the fork that lanes never work in.
2. Vendor or bundle the quota module with the aggregator so no external checkout is on the runtime path.
3. At minimum: fail loud — a tick that dies at import should surface somewhere other than a heartbeat file (the stall went unnoticed for hours).

Do NOT fix by switching/cleaning `~/git/openchamber-fork` in place: it holds another lane's dirty queue work (queue/8357-224).

Found during the 2026-11-04 laptop-session coordinator run (Phase 2 of the #5704 verification — that fix itself is landed via PR #5719; the timer stays red until this issue is resolved).

items.title: Workhorse route: every leg quota-walled at once — no relief leg outside the exhausted pools (fleet stalled)

## Symptom

2026-11-09 evening: the fleet went to zero active sessions. Fleet-minder census: 60 live sessions failed on quota — 30× Mistral Vibe 402 (budget exhausted), 29× CommandCode 429 (weekly limit, resets Tue 2026-11-10T06:52:52Z). Two minder failover-prompt kicks went ACTIVE, then re-failed in ~90 s on the same walled head. Workhorse route decisions returned `no-candidates` ~2,500 times in 2 h.

## Diagnosis (verified on the wire, 2026-11-10T00:15–00:50Z)

This was **not** the cured #7991 auth wall (zero auth errors). Every member of the workhorse route is genuinely at its plan limit at the same time — each verified from the provider's own error and the fresh quota record (generatedAt 2026-11-10T00:15:01Z):

- Flash pool: OpenCode Go 429 "Go usage limit exceeded", retry-after ≈ 6 d (weekly → Nov 16); ClinePass quota-gated → Nov 13; OpenDesign quota-gated → Nov 14; CommandCode weekly → Nov 10 06:52Z (retry-after honored by its bench); Mistral Vibe 402 budget exhausted.
- Luna: openai.main weekly 100% → Nov 13; openai.alternate 5h 100% → 04:26Z.
- Spark (Meta): 429 "Subscription quota exhausted", retry-after 518610 s → Nov 16.
- Antigravity Gemini: 429 "Individual quota reached", weekly 100% → Nov 13 23:43Z.

The minder's named "candidates with headroom" audited:

- `_claude` — NOT a candidate. Its quota read is a stale 2026-11-07 snapshot (the heartbeat errors); the credential is blanked and its leaves sit on auth benches. The "7d 61%" figure is frozen data.
- Antigravity **Claude** — REAL headroom (per-model weekly 63%, 5h 14%, live successes all evening) but seated only in the deliberate tiers — **not in workhorse**. That gap is the routing defect: when every pooled leg walled together, workhorse had no relief leg outside the exhausted pools, so correct `no-candidates` decisions stalled the fleet.

## Fix landed

- Config: `_antigravity/claude-sonnet-5-5#high` seated as the fourth member of `workhorse-weighted` (direct leaf, weight 10 — the pattern of the Gemini leaf Drew seated in this stage 2026-11-07; Drew's 2026-10-31 Antigravity removal was from the primary path, over Gemini-bucket burn).

## Problem

The 2026-10-31 22:40 CDT code lane wave lost 5 of its 6 root sessions terminally when the workhorse route reached a quota-exhausted leg, instead of the route rotating those sessions to a live leg.

Content-verified from the laptop OpenChamber API (`/api/session/<id>/message`) by the conductor cycle 2026-10-31 22:52 CDT:

- Failed roots (all `opencode-route/workhorse`, Queue lane code 22:40): ses_e5e6ace9855ffeRyqRUjjNVoeg, ses_e5e6ace9f3affe0Xg8PG6Ytl5H, ses_e5e6acea082ffe20Y7BWyRJVaq, ses_e5e6acea3f2ffeDkwnSH52qMIm, ses_e5e6acea9b5ffeCBemgz5smt7h
- Every one contains `provider.rate-limit` 429: "Subscription quota exhausted. Your usage window resets at 2026-11-02T00:00:00Z." on the muse-spark leg; one also shows `provider.internal` 502 "Direct Meta route request failed: fetch failed" (muse-direct).
- Zero `provider.auth` hits and zero thought_signature hits — this is NOT a recurrence of #3216.
- In the same sessions, earlier attempts on another leg (gpt terra via openai) produced normal assistant turns, so a live alternative existed while the sessions died on the exhausted leg.
- The sixth code root and all other lanes' 22:40 roots succeeded.

## Why it matters

A quota-exhausted leg is routine (pools are expected to run out before reset when alternatives exist). A route that lets the session die on the exhausted leg instead of falling through turns a routine pool state into lost lane work and burned attempts.

## Acceptance criteria

- A 429 quota-exhausted response from a route leg is treated as a leg failure and the session's next attempt falls through to the next live leg in the route, without terminating the session.
- A 502/fetch-failed on a direct leg likewise falls through rather than ending the session where another leg is available.
- Verified by a route attempt ledger / session transcript showing a session surviving a quota-exhausted leg and completing on an alternative leg.
